Local Tastes
Mexican Red Chile
Red chile sauces and stews appear across menus here. Chile rellenos and enchiladas rojas are standard items at most Sedona Mexican restaurants.
Elote Cafe · Mesa Grill
Mesquite-Grilled Foods
Mesquite wood native to the Arizona desert gives a smoky flavor to grilled meats. Many local restaurants feature mesquite-grilled specialties on their menus.
Mariposa Latin Inspired Grill · Canyon Breeze
Prickly Pear
Prickly pear fruit and pads appear in salads, sauces, and margaritas across the city. The flavor is mildly sweet with slight tartness and a vivid magenta color.
Tlaquepaque Arts Village · Uptown restaurants
Arizona Wine
Sedona sits near the Verde Valley AVA. Local tasting rooms serve Grenache, Tempranillo, and other varietals grown in the high desert mountains.
Javelina Leap Winery · Page Springs Cellars

Worth Knowing

A Cliff Dwelling Misnamed, a Village Built From Scratch

Montezuma Castle has nothing to do with Montezuma. Soldiers who came through the Verde Valley in 1864 saw the five-story cliff dwelling and, familiar with the Aztec empire from the Mexican War, assumed only an Aztec civilization could have built something so advanced — so they named it after the Aztec emperor. The structure was actually built between 1100 and 1350 by the Sinagua, a farming people with no connection to the Aztecs, and Montezuma himself almost certainly never set foot anywhere near Arizona. The name stuck anyway and the National Park Service still uses it today.

Tlaquepaque, by contrast, was never trying to be an ancient ruin — it was built to look like one. Nevada developer Abe Miller spent two years persuading the landowners to sell him their sycamore grove, promising to build around the trees rather than clear them, then hired an architect who took him on a research trip through small-town Mexico before laying a single brick. The construction crew was made up of amateur, self-taught plasterers given full creative freedom — if they weren't happy with a wall, Miller let them tear it down and redo it. The result, opened in 1973, was designed from the start to feel decades older than it is.
